primitives.name: Rumor Propagation Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: The paper proposes FTR-18, a multilingual (English/Spanish/Portuguese) dataset of transfer news + Twitter reactions, and frames the full rumour-classification pipeline from Zubiaga et al.: rumour detection, rumour tracking, stance classification, veracity classification, and evidence retrieval.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'R(t)': 'Rumour intensity at time t (dimensionless)', 'T': 'Temporal domain of rumour propagation (days)', 'L': 'Language modality index (English=1, Spanish=2, Portuguese=3)'}
primitives.assumptions: Rumour propagation follows a Markovian temporal process with language-specific transition probabilities.
primitives.breakdown_regime: At T = 0, R(t) = 0; at T = T_window, R(t) resolves to binary veracity.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's rumour tracking kernel where R(t) corresponds to player movement likelihood over time.
layer2.telemetry: Cross-platform tweet volume and article frequency as proxy for R(t).

primitives.name: Hedging Language Lexicon
primitives.verbatim_quote: It asks what linguistic structures journalists use to report unverified transfers (attribution hedging, question headlines, cascading conditional moves).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'H': 'Hedging strength index (0 to 1)', 'Q': 'Question-headline indicator (binary)', 'C': 'Conditional move count (integer)'}
primitives.assumptions: Hedging increases with uncertainty in transfer veracity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: H approaches 1 when Q = 1 or C > 0; H = 0 for definitive reporting.

layer2.mapping: Derived from GSI's linguistic pattern recognition engine to classify rumour veracity.
layer2.telemetry: Frequency of hedging phrases in news articles.

primitives.name: Veracity Annotation Scheme
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Veracity annotation: resolved after the window via official UEFA registration — True if the transfer happened as rumoured, False otherwise (a natural ground truth).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'V': 'Veracity label (True/False)', 'T_w': 'Transfer window duration (days)', 'G': 'Ground truth resolution (UEFA registration)'}
primitives.assumptions: V is a deterministic function of G within T_w.
primitives.breakdown_regime: V = 1 if G confirms rumour; V = 0 otherwise.

layer2.mapping: Analogous to GSE's injury rumor validation using official medical reports.
layer2.telemetry: Percentage of confirmed vs. unconfirmed rumours post-window.

primitives.name: Attribution Hedging Lexicon
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Documented hedging patterns: "according to reports/sources," "player P linked to club C," "reports suggest," "source S reported" (often without link), question headlines ("Ronaldo out, Neymar in at Real Madrid?"), cascading conditional moves ("club will sell X to fund Y").
primitives.assumptions: Hedging signals intent to disclaim direct confirmation.

primitives.name: Cross-Media Echo Propagation
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Qualitative findings: pervasive attribution hedging, echo effect (outlets re-reporting third-party rumours as news), question-headlines concentrated in Spanish media, cascading conditional-move narratives that sustain audience attention across follow-ups.
primitives.assumptions: Echoes propagate without introducing new independent evidence.
